## AIG reaffirms our commitment to the wholesale market, expanding our capabilities and identifying innovative solutions at the Lexington Producer Conference.

At the 2026 Lexington Producer Conference, AIG underscored our commitment to the wholesale market, expanding our capabilities around the needs of our wholesale partners, and solving more of our clients’ complex risk needs.


Held October 26–28 in South Carolina, the conference centered on the theme “Meeting the Moment in an Evolving Market,” bringing together AIG colleagues and our wholesale broker partners for a wide-ranging discussion about opportunities for innovative solutions across AI and digital infrastructure in the Excess and Surplus (E&S) market and the important role E&S plays in the industry – with our broker partners at the center of what we do.


During a fireside chat, AIG leaders highlighted our underwriting expertise, commitment to our wholesale model, and ability to connect AIG across products and geographies to more holistically strengthen our relationships and our shared goals for growth.


### “We want to be an insurer that a client can look at and say ‘they can help me with just about everything,’” AIG President & Chief Executive Officer[Eric Andersen](https://www.aig.com/home/about/leadership-and-governance/eric-andersen) said.


Working with brokers to identify needs and develop solutions is central to Lexington’s approach, said[Lou Levinson](https://www.lexingtoninsurance.com/home/risk-solutions/our-team/lou-levinson) , Lexington’s CEO and President of AIG Wholesale, North America Commercial Insurance.


“Being able to solve so many problems under one brand is such a unique thing that we’re incredibly proud of,” said Lou, who joined Eric in the discussion.


[Lexington Insurance Company](https://www.lexingtoninsurance.com/home/about-us) is AIG’s U.S.-based E&S insurance business, designing tailored property and casualty coverage for complex or unusual risks that standard insurance markets may not cover. Its wholesale-only distribution model combines Lexington’s underwriting and claims expertise with specialist brokers’ market knowledge.


Its new Life Sciences team in Core Casualty and Financial Institutions practices in LexPro are examples of capabilities designed to bring tailored liability solutions to more small- and mid-sized businesses through wholesale partners.


## Looking ahead in the evolving market


During the conversation, Eric offered insights on balancing growth with underwriting discipline and supporting partners through both favorable and challenging market conditions. Lexington’s financial strength and claims capabilities underpin that long-term commitment.


“We want to make sure that the marketplace knows that we’re in it for the long term,” Eric said.


During the conference, our broker partners also heard from Steven Jones, AIG’s Global Head of Data Science and AI, who led a session on applying AI to an evolving risk landscape. He explored how technology can help to enhance AIG’s underwriting and claims services by helping teams make better decisions and respond faster, helping drive business outcomes. Bill Flannery, AIG’s Assistant Director, ERM Operations, Governance and Reporting, joined Lew Lukens, Senior Partner, Signum Global Advisors, for a discussion of global trends reshaping the business.


The conversations also examined emerging client exposures, including AI, data infrastructure and professional liability risks, and opportunities for new coverage solutions.
